Curriculum & Pathways

Nigeria has two main routes into the nursing profession. Both lead to registration with the Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria (NMCN), but they differ in structure and academic outcome.

Awarded byColleges of Nursing Sciences (NBTE-accredited)
Duration4 years, non-terminal, with concentrated clinical experience (SIWES) toward the end
CertificateLegally recognised academic diploma (ND/HND) + professional licence
Admission5 O'level credits incl. English, Biology, Chemistry, Physics, Maths; UTME usually required
After graduationNMCN professional exam for RN licence; HND graduates need a PGD before MSc Nursing
Full course structure (ND I–II, HND I–II)
Awarded byUniversities with NUC-accredited Nursing departments
Duration5 years + 1 year internship (Direct Entry from RN status can start at 200 level)
CertificateBachelor of Nursing Science (BNSc) degree + professional licence
AdmissionUTME with same core science subjects, or Direct Entry for existing RNs
After graduationNMCN professional exam for RN licence; can proceed directly to MSc Nursing, no PGD needed
Full course structure (200–500 Level)
Both pathways sit under NMCN's benchmark minimum standards, and both end in the same NMCN Professional Examination (CBT + clinical/practical skills assessment) for licensure.
